comparativeCohorts.independentJudgment: Prioritize OnPoint, SACHR and NJHRC for concentrated severe-risk contact, direct treatment/supply paths and operational contrasts. Other peers remain plausible but broader portfolios, public supply substitution, parent subsidy or educational reach make marginal donor health gains less legible. No claim of measured EV dominance.

BVMI/Parker offer explicit uninsured eligibility and volunteer leverage to test; Charles B Wang adds a specific hepatitis linkage hypothesis. Broader reimbursed clinic systems and foundation transfer pathways need greater accounting/clinical additionality work before priority, not rejection as ineffective.

NYLPI/NYLAG/MFJ have explicit health-access or psychiatric-housing chains; CHPC offers a high-variance scalable safe-basement policy test. Other legal/housing organizations have broader case mix, network accounting or weaker initial health conversion. Policy and legal recoveries are not themselves health benefits.

GLWD concentrates on illness-tailored food; HWCLI offers local completed-navigation hypothesis without primarily food logistics. Other food banks, benefit navigators, foundation and elder-support agencies remain comparators; whole costs, reimbursement and health-versus-transfer gains decide later ranking.

Samaritans is selected for volunteer-supported local crisis response as research hypothesis. Larger national/clinical/settlement portfolios, affiliate accounting and reliance on reimbursed capacity put peers behind it provisionally. No hotline call is assumed to avert a death; Fountain House remains eligible existing organization.

Sanctuary prioritizes integrated high-risk legal/trauma/safety intervention. Other survivor and youth-housing providers remain serious alternates; shelter unit cost, durable exits, public substitution and subcontracted clinical attribution are decisive unresolved comparisons.

Common Justice, NCST and KAVI create distinct violent-felony diversion, community/hospital and bedside reinjury tests. CASES/Fortune/Osborne/GOSO/LIFE Camp are credible peers but public treatment funding or broader nonclinical portfolios leave more initial dilution questions. Crime trends/testimonials do not establish causal effects.

TA has narrow NYC street implementation; WE ACT/NYCEJA and NJEJA/ICC offer concrete air/heat/exposure pathways on both sides of state line. Open Plans/TSTC/RPA broaden geography/portfolio; cycling classes, general water protection and AEA weatherization face larger health-conversion or public-contract uncertainties. Selected coalition benefits must be divided, never summed as independent wins.

CGE emphasizes high-risk maternal addiction barrier removal; NMPP adds concentrated Harlem prenatal/infant navigation. PHS/CAMBA/CHS/consortia/general prevention remain eligible but grant pass-through, broad organizational spending or referral-only activity weaken initial marginal-health visibility.

CIDNY selected for explicit safe transition and benefits chain with potentially durable functional benefit. Vision rehabilitation, specialized education and other ILCs remain comparators; public entitlement substitution, affiliate costs and verified functional outcomes are unresolved.
